# AVR boards and UART — 0.30

Supported: Uno R3, classic Nano (ATmega328P, 5V /16MHz), Pro Mini ATmega328P (5V /16MHz). Shared instruction engine, 32KB flash /2KB SRAM, Timer0/1/2, USART0, SPI and TWI. Nano and Pro Mini expose ADC6/ADC7 as analog-only channels: no GPIO/pullup/PWM/edge capture there. Nano Every, Nano ESP32, Uno R4 and 3.3V /8MHz Pro Mini are different targets and are not included.

Canonical board pad definitions control geometry/net validation/ground/reset aliases, DC rails and ADC source inputs. Nano uses the official 30-pin order and 45×18mm outline. Pro Mini pad coordinates and header aliases were extracted from SparkFun's published Eagle board, including FTDI/inner analog pads. The original SVG artwork is simplified; it is not a photorealistic package or mechanical tolerance model. Nano breadboard mounting and mechanical body collision are not enabled in this release. Power rails are ideal 5V/3.3V; RAW/VIN regulator, FTDI reset pulse, USB controller and bootloader execution are not modeled.

Compiler defines the selected ARDUINO_AVR_UNO/NANO/PRO target; Nano/Pro Mini use the eight-input Arduino variant definition. CPU is unchanged ATmega328P. Conservative firmware limits: Uno32256 /Nano30720 /Pro Mini30720 bytes; 2048 static SRAM. Firmware cache/source fingerprint includes board identity; cross-board cached or imported firmware is rejected. Imported raw HEX has no embedded board identification: manual import assigns the current selected target.

UART TX frames begin at actual USART UDR writes. Period is (UBRR+1)×8/16 CPU cycles; 5..8 data bits LSB-first, even/odd parity and1/2 stop bits. TX/RX edges enter the canonical DC network with50Ω finite drivers and the GPIO analyzer through actual PIN registers. Native AVR8js byte transport remains the low-level RX register/IRQ delivery endpoint. External pin sampling supplies the byte once, preventing parallel byte and pin sensor responses. Physical framing/parity errors set USART flags; 9-bit and synchronous USART are outside this adapter.

The receiver samples start at0.5bit, then data/parity/stop centers. Events execute at AVR instruction boundaries, so edge/sample times have instruction quantization. Native AVR8js USART buffering/overrun is limited; no full two-stage hardware FIFO, oscillator jitter or metastability. UART peripheral TX reserves D1 while TX enabled. Terminal RX input and MH-Z19B use the same electrical framing model; multiple sensor TX sources on one net report conflict. Reconfiguration/power loss/topology change/dispose cancel pending frame epochs.

Actual Arduino AVR1.8.7 SoftwareSerial source is compiled as a separate firmware translation unit when included, with original LGPL headers and archive retained. It runs normal GPIO instructions and pin-change interrupts, not parsed source patterns. One active SoftwareSerial listener as upstream library supports. MH-Z19B is9600 8N1; it discovers RX/TX on the wired GPIO nets and returns a checksum-valid response20ms after a valid command frame. Incorrect wiring/power/framing cannot produce a valid packet.

Sources: [Nano pinout](https://docs.arduino.cc/resources/pinouts/A000005-full-pinout.pdf), [Pro Mini board CAD](https://github.com/sparkfun/Arduino_Pro_Mini_328/blob/master/Hardware/Arduino-Pro-Mini.brd), [Arduino AVR1.8.7](https://github.com/arduino/ArduinoCore-avr/tree/1.8.7/libraries/SoftwareSerial), [AVR8js](https://github.com/wokwi/avr8js).

Next separate target: Mega2560 with avr6 toolchain/core objects, 256KB flash/8KB SRAM, full port map, six timers and four USARTs; then ESP32 with Xtensa or RISC-V compiler/CPU/runtime. Current AVR firmware is never presented as either of these processors.
